#Web Audio

AudioContext, OfflineAudioContext, their nodes and decodeAudioData. What a script sees is JavaScript (native/js/odin/web_audio.js, evaluated the first time a realm of a window reads one of the interfaces: a page that never asks pays nothing). The graph, its threads and every computation are the browser's: src/webaudio, a package with no JavaScript in it and its own unit tests. src/page/bindings_webaudio.odin and api/webaudio.widl are between the two.

#The render graph

A node is a number of a graph; a graph is a host object of the page. The page's thread and the render thread share the graph under one lock, which the render thread holds for one quantum (128 frames) at a time.

  • A running AudioContext has one thread and one media.Audio_Output (backend_audio_output: WASAPI on Windows, cpal on Linux, the null output with WREN_AUDIO_OUTPUT=null or no device). The thread keeps the output's queue at the latency asked for, a quantum at a time: the device's clock paces the rendering, and so currentTime. Suspending ends the thread and closes the stream.
  • An OfflineAudioContext has a thread until its rendering is over, as fast as it goes. suspend(t) stops it at a quantum (rounded up) until resume().
  • The order of processing is recomputed when connections change: every node runs, a source with nowhere to go still ends and an analyser still listens. A cycle goes through a DelayNode (read at its turn, written at the end of the quantum: at least a quantum of delay), or is muted.
  • A node leaves its graph when its JavaScript object has been collected and nothing can come out of it: no input, no source at work, a delay's or convolver's tail over. Thousands of one-shot sounds leave nothing behind. (A cycle whose objects are all gone stays until the context closes.)

A page leaving or a tab closing destroys its graphs with its objects: the thread is joined there. The render thread gives the page's thread ids, never pointers (Web_Audio_Token).

#Buffers: what a Float32Array is, and what the render sees

Each realm's memory is a Wasm instance, which the render thread does not read. An AudioBuffer has its samples in one of two places:

  • getChannelData gives a real Float32Array of the realm, made on first asking;
  • the browser has an immutable-while-shared block (Pcm), which graphs hold references to.

start() (and buffer = after it, and a convolver's buffer =) is the specification's "acquire the content": the arrays' samples go to the browser, only when they differ from what is there, and a block that a graph is playing is copied first. From then on the script's arrays are its own, and getChannelData makes new ones: what is written to the old ones is not heard. An array transferred away makes the buffer play nothing. A buffer from decodeAudioData or a rendering stays in the browser until a script reads it, so a game's decoded sounds cost the realm nothing.

#Autoplay

media.autoplay.policy: allow-all starts a context at once; allow-muted and block leave it suspended until the page has had a click or a key press (the same sticky activation as media elements), at which point every context that wants to run starts, with or without another resume(). Its pending resume() promises settle then.

The tab's mute silences the contexts' outputs without the page knowing, and a context that gives sound shows the tab's speaker.

#decodeAudioData

A blocking thread of the page's pool decodes the whole file, then converts it to the context's rate (a windowed sinc). MP4 and WebM go through the demuxers of src/media; WAV (PCM, float, A-law, mu-law), MP3, ADTS AAC, FLAC and Ogg (Opus, Vorbis) are cut into packets in src/webaudio/decode.odin, and the packets go to the decoders of src/media: Media Foundation on Windows, Symphonia and libopus on Linux. Vorbis has no decoder on Windows. The argument is detached at the call, as specified.

#What each node does

Interface
AudioParamevery automation method, a-rate and k-rate; events inside a value curve throw NotSupportedError; connections add to the value
AudioBufferSourceNodeloop, playbackRate, detune, offset, duration, sub-sample start, negative rates; linear interpolation
OscillatorNodesine computed, the others and PeriodicWave from band-limited tables (three per octave); silent at Nyquist and above
GainNode, ConstantSourceNode, DelayNode, StereoPannerNode, ChannelSplitterNode, ChannelMergerNodeas specified
BiquadFilterNode, IIRFilterNodedirect form I in doubles; getFrequencyResponse
PannerNodeequal-power, distance and cone models; panningModel = "HRTF" is accepted and pans the same way
DynamicsCompressorNodethe knee and ratio of the specification, a 6 ms look-ahead, an attack and release envelope (not Chromium's adaptive release)
WaveShaperNodethe curve at the context's rate: oversample is kept and does nothing
AnalyserNodeall four reads, smoothing, Blackman window
ConvolverNodeuniform partitioned convolution with no latency, 1, 2 and 4 channels. A very long impulse response (over about 10 s) may be more than a quantum's time
ScriptProcessorNodeblocks to the page and back through rings, two blocks of delay; an offline rendering waits for the page's answer
AudioWorkletNodesee below: process() in a realm of its own, parameters, port, processorerror, realtime and offline
MediaElementAudioSourceNodethe player sends what it plays to the node, with the element's volume, and the speakers get silence. The media clock goes on

#AudioWorklet

context.audioWorklet.addModule(url) starts the context's realm the first time: a JavaScript worker of the document, its own Wasm instance on a thread of its own (worker.odin, counted in workers.max_per_page and workers.max_total), with a worklet's scope (native/js/odin/web_audio_worklet.js): AudioWorkletGlobalScope, registerProcessor, currentFrame, currentTime, sampleRate, AudioWorkletProcessor, and of what a worker has only what is exposed to worklets. Modules are import()ed there, by requests relayed to the page's thread under the document's policies. AudioWorkletNode, its port and parameters are in web_audio.js; the page and the realm talk with the worker's messages, so processorOptions and ports are structured clones.

A node's quantum is a request to that thread (src/webaudio/worklet.odin), since the render thread cannot read a Wasm instance's memory:

  • the input channels and the param values are copied to the context's one exchange buffer, the realm's thread is woken, and the render thread waits, Graph.mu let go, so the page never waits for a processor;
  • the realm reads them into Float32Arrays it keeps per processor (new ones when the channels change or the script transferred a buffer), calls process(), and the output comes back the same way. Nothing allocates on the render thread once the buffer has its size, and the realm allocates only what its script does;
  • a realtime quantum waits half of what is queued ahead of the device, between 5 and 100 ms, an offline one webaudio.worklet_stall_ms. Past that the quantum is silence and the next ones do not wait until the realm has caught up: what it was running is dropped. The microtasks of the realm run once per quantum, after all its processors;
  • a throw in process() or in a constructor is processorerror, with the message, on that node, which then gives silence. A realm that stops (a trap, out of memory), or stays busy past webaudio.worklet_stall_ms and is then stopped by the page, is processorerror on every node. process() that never returns costs that silence and that delay, never a hung render thread: closing a page or a context interrupts the wait and joins the render thread first.

A node is kept while its processor is at work (process() returned true). A context collected or closed stops its realm.

Each context with a worklet has its realm: an instance and a thread (about what a worker costs). One realm serves one context, where the specification has one global scope per context as well.

#What there is not

  • AudioWorklet's corners: import() also works inside a worklet's modules (the specification rejects it); an error thrown that is not an Error (throw "text") has no line and no file in its event; AudioParamMap's values are real params, but a getter a script puts on Object.prototype for a param's name is not read (audioworkletprocessor-param-getter-overridden).
  • MediaStreamAudioSourceNode, MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode, createMediaStreamTrackSource: Wren has no MediaStream.
  • HRTF panning; setSinkId (sinkId reads "", the default device); playbackStats, AudioRenderCapacity.
  • Other render quantum sizes: renderSizeHint is ignored, renderQuantumSize is 128.
  • Incremental offline rendering (startRendering(chunk), close(), a context with no length), a recent addition.

#Preferences

webaudio.enabled, webaudio.latency_ms (latencyHint "interactive"; "balanced" is twice that, "playback" four times), webaudio.sample_rate, webaudio.max_buffer_mb, webaudio.max_contexts, webaudio.worklet_stall_ms.

#Tests

odin test src/webaudio (known values: a sine's samples, ramps, a biquad against the cookbook's formulas, convolution, WAV decoding, the thread on the null output); examples/jsweb/webaudio.js and webaudio_autoplay.js (jsweb, src/tools/e2e/web_jsweb.odin); build\wpt.exe -only /webaudio; examples/site/webaudio.html for a person, or a driven Wren reading its AnalyserNode.
